question: What salary do I need to get a Swedish work permit?
reference_answer: The salary must be at least 90 percent of the median salary in Sweden at the time of application (6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen). Salary, insurance and other terms must also be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the occupation or industry, and for a stay of up to one year the person must have, or have applied for, comprehensive health insurance valid in Sweden.
notes: Section last amended by Lag (2026:295). Check its in-force date and transitional provisions in SFSR: a candidate for a version-dependent item in phase 4. Add the Migrationsverket salary page as an alternative in the same group once web units exist.

question: What does 6 kap. 2 a § utlänningslagen say?
reference_answer: A work permit under 6 kap. 2 § första stycket may be granted for at most two years, and not for longer than the employment. It is tied to a specific employer and a specific type of work. After a total permit period of two years it is tied only to the type of work.

question: Can I get permanent residence after working in Sweden?
reference_answer: It depends on the permit history, so the first response should ask which permits the person has had and for how long. Permanent residence may be granted to someone who has had a residence permit for work (or research, an EU Blue Card, an ICT permit or a seasonal work permit) for a total of four years during the last seven (5 kap. 5 §). Time with a work permit after a rejected asylum application does not count. The person must also be able to support themselves, and there must be no doubt, given their expected conduct, that the permit should be granted (5 kap. 7 §).
notes: Two required groups: the qualifying period (5 §) and the special requirements (7 §).

question: I have a two-year work permit. Can my spouse or partner move here and also work in Sweden?
reference_answer: Yes, normally. The spouse or partner of someone with a work permit can be granted a residence permit under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen, if the person in Sweden can support themselves and the spouse (the level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting the spouse too, 4 kap. 4 c §; exceptions for special reasons). The permit is valid for the same period as the work permit. A person with a temporary residence permit may be given a work permit under 6 kap. 3 § utlänningslagen, unless reasons related to the purpose of the residence permit speak against it; Migrationsverket's page says adult family members are permitted to work.
notes: Check utlänningsförordningen for further conditions on family members of work-permit holders, and whether 17 a § (maintenance) applies here; 17 a and 17 b were not read when drafting. Legal basis re-checked 2026-11-24 (phase 5 step 1): a work-permit holder's family is granted permits under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen (maintenance requirement, level in 4 c §, no housing-size requirement, same validity as the work permit), not 5 kap. 3 a § utlänningslagen as first written.

question: How long do I need to live in Sweden to get EU long-term resident status?
reference_answer: Five years without interruption in Sweden with a residence permit or otherwise as lawfully resident (5 a kap. 1 §). Stays for temporary reasons or for studies do not count. Absences shorter than six consecutive months, and no more than ten months in total during the five years, do not break the period.

question: What does an employer have to do before a non-EU employee can apply for a Swedish work permit?
reference_answer: The law only requires that the recruitment complies with Sweden's EU commitments (6 kap. 2 § andra stycket utlänningslagen). The practical steps are Migrationsverket's requirements: advertise the job in Sweden and the EU, make an offer of employment, ask the relevant union for its opinion on the terms, and start the application from the employer side, after which the employee completes their part.
notes: From a real case (Case 1). Verify on the employer pages: the minimum advertising period (10 days in the case) and the channels (Platsbanken / EURES).

question: Does the trade union have to give its opinion before a work permit application can go ahead, and what happens if it never answers?
reference_answer: The union statement is Migrationsverket's requirement, not the law's. The employer sends the union information about the employment and asks for its opinion on the terms. If the union has not commented within 14 days, the employer can go on with the application without waiting for it; Migrationsverket then checks the terms against the collective agreement and wage statistics itself.

question: I'm in Sweden on a residence permit as the family member of a student, and it expires soon. Can I apply for a work permit from inside Sweden?
reference_answer: The main rule is to apply and be granted a permit before entering Sweden (5 kap. 18 § första stycket utlänningslagen); the exceptions are listed in the following paragraphs. None of them clearly covers a student's family member switching to a work permit, so whether an application made in Sweden is accepted is Migrationsverket's assessment (possibly 'synnerliga skäl', 18 § andra stycket 11). The answer should say the rules don't settle it, explain the main rule, and advise applying before the current permit expires.

question: Can I keep working while my first work permit application is being processed?
reference_answer: It depends on the current permit and the basis of the application, so the first response should ask. If the current permit, with its own right to work, is still valid, work can continue under it. Once it expires, the ordinance's exemption for pending applications (5 kap. 2 b § utlänningsförordningen) applies only to applications made inside Sweden under 5 kap. 18 § andra stycket 8 b or fjärde stycket utlänningslagen, and only with that employer and type of work, until the decision.
notes: From a real case (Case 1): the old permit expired in April 2025 and the person kept working for about seven months while waiting. Check which rule allowed that, on Migrationsverket's page.

question: I've been laid off. How long do I have to find a new job before my work permit is affected, and from when does that time count?
reference_answer: The permit may be revoked when the employment has ended, unless within three months you get a new job covered by the permit, or apply for a work permit for a new job and that application is later granted (7 kap. 3 § första stycket 2 utlänningslagen). It is a 'may', not an automatic expiry. Migrationsverket counts the three months from the last day of employment, not from when notice is given. The three months do not extend your permit: they apply only while it is still valid. A new job may need a new work-permit application, depending on the employer and on whether the permit is limited to a profession.
notes: From a real case (Case 2). Verify the counting rule on Migrationsverket's page. Page confirms: three months from the last working day, while the permit is still valid. Reference answer aligned 2026-11-24 with the reviewed multi-job-ends-903 (review on the review page).

question: I have a valid work permit tied to my old employer and have found a new job. Do I apply for a new work permit or for an extension?
reference_answer: Your permit is tied to your current employer, so you need a work permit for the new job before you work there. Migrationsverket's page calls this a new work-permit application; in law it is an extension with a new employment (6 kap. 4 a § utlänningslagen: the new job must meet 2 § första stycket and also andra stycket), and in Migrationsverket's e-service it is made through the extension route while your current permit is valid. You can start working for the new employer once you have applied, before the decision, provided you applied before your current permit expired; the new employer must have advertised the job in Sweden and the EU/EEA and Switzerland first.
notes: From a real case (Case 2): the option was confusing; Migrationsverket's phone service said to choose extension (D23: notes only). Verify on the change-of-employer page. question: My previous employer didn't take out all the insurances it should have. Can that stop my work permit extension?
reference_answer: It can. An extension must be refused if there were grounds to revoke the earlier permit because its conditions, which include insurance, were not met for a reason other than the job ending (6 kap. 4 a § andra stycket 4 and 7 kap. 7 e § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen). But a permit need not be revoked in minor cases or where revocation would not be reasonable (7 kap. 7 e § tredje stycket), which 4 a § says to take into account. Whether a particular gap is minor is Migrationsverket's assessment, so the answer must say the outcome isn't settled by the sources.
notes: From a real case (Cases 1 and 2). The legal link between an employer's missing insurances and a later extension.

question: I had some periods between jobs (the three-month job-search time) while on a work permit. Do they count toward the four years needed for permanent residence?
reference_answer: The law counts time with a residence permit for work, four years in total during the last seven (5 kap. 5 § första stycket utlänningslagen), not time in employment; on its wording, a valid permit during a job search is permit time. How Migrationsverket treats such periods, and whether the permit conditions must have been met throughout, is practice and possibly case law, so the answer must say the sources it has don't settle it.

question: If my application for permanent residence is refused, what happens to the work permit extension I applied for at the same time?
reference_answer: The two are decided separately. Migrationsverket's pages: if you are not granted a permanent residence permit, you keep your temporary permit; if permanent residence is refused but a temporary permit is granted, you can in some cases apply for permanent residence the next time you extend; if the extension is also refused, you must prepare to leave the country, and the decision says how to appeal. In law the extension is assessed on its own conditions (6 kap. 4 a § utlänningslagen), including that it must be refused if the earlier permit could have been revoked because its conditions were not met, unless the case is minor or revocation would not be reasonable (6 kap. 4 a § andra stycket 4, 7 kap. 7 e §).
notes: From a real case (Case 3). Expectation reviewed 2026-11-26 against Migrationsverket's pages as seen on 2026-11-20. Was not-settled ("the joint handling is practice"); two pages now describe it (the extension page and the page on a decision about permanent residence), so it is a lookup and both are expected sources.

question: My spouse is here on a family permit tied to my work permit and has no job. Can my spouse get permanent residence when I do?
reference_answer: Possibly, but normally not without an income of their own. You and your spouse can apply for permanent residence at the same time; Migrationsverket assesses your application first and, if you are granted permanent residence, then your spouse's. question: What does 6 a kap. 1 § utlänningslagen require for an EU Blue Card?
reference_answer: An employment contract for highly qualified employment in Sweden of at least six months, with a salary of at least 1.25 times the average gross annual salary in Sweden at the time of application; pay, insurance and other terms no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice; comprehensive health insurance for stays of up to one year; and recruitment compatible with Sweden's EU commitments. Highly qualified means completed studies of 180 higher-education credits or five years of comparable professional experience; for a regulated profession, the right to practise in Sweden must be shown.
notes: Drafted from the statute text. Also a time-dependent candidate: the salary threshold is a multiple of a figure that changes yearly.

question: My decision letter refers to 7 kap. 7 e § utlänningslagen. What does that section say?
reference_answer: A temporary residence permit for work must be revoked if the work permit conditions in 6 kap. 2 § första stycket are no longer met for a reason other than the employment ending, or if the person hasn't started work within four months of the permit's first day of validity. If the employment ends after the person was told a revocation investigation had started, the job-loss rule applies with four months instead of three. A permit need not be revoked in minor cases or where revocation would not be reasonable.
notes: Drafted from the statute text. Linked to the insurance-gap questions (204, 304).

question: What is 6 kap. 2 b § utlänningslagen about?
reference_answer: It excludes two groups from the ordinary work permit under 6 kap. 2 § första stycket: someone employed by a company outside the EEA and Switzerland who is transferred for more than 90 days as a manager, specialist or trainee to a company in the same group in Sweden or another EU state (they need an ICT permit under 6 b kap.), and someone with a fixed-term contract as a seasonal worker with an employer established in Sweden (they need a seasonal work permit under 6 c kap.). Both exclusions have exceptions for categories listed in 6 b kap. 3 § and 6 c kap. 4 §.
